sections.text: Serenity, kindness, silence, self-control and purity - this is austerity of mind.
These threefold austerities performed with faith, and without thought of reward, may truly be accounted Pure.
Austerity coupled with hypocrisy or performed for the sake of self-glorification, popularity or vanity, comes from Passion, and its result is always doubtful and temporary.

We had been discussing chapter 17, Shraddha Vibhaga Yoga, three types of Shraddha. We are coming to the concluding portion of the Bhagavad Gita, and some of us who started from chapter one and have gone through all 16 chapters may start wondering: what about the people who never get a chance to learn the Bhagavad Gita? We are fortunate that we get a chance to learn the Bhagavad Gita one way or another. But what about the people who never thought about learning it or never had a chance? The thought does come to our mind: how do they live their life in a manner which is appropriate? A similar question Arjuna asked in the beginning of this chapter.
Arjuna says: I learned from you all this knowledge which you have given me, and I have Shraddha. But how about the people who have never gone through the scriptures or had the guidance from the scriptures? They also have Shraddha -- everyone has Shraddha in something, that we know. So how is their Shraddha helping them, or how do you classify their Shraddha? What kind of Shraddha is that, without any basis or guidance from any guru or scriptures?
And Bhagavan said each person has a Shraddha according to his or her mental makeup. It as simple as that. Whatever my mental makeup is that will decide what type of things I will be convinced will give me happiness. Bhavan said that there are three types of Shraddha you find in people. One is Sattvik, other is Rajasic, third is Tamasic depending on the texture of the persons mind. We know that texture of our mind changes as the circumstances change.
So depending on my circumstances and the basic nature of my mind, my mind will be either in a Sattvic mode or in a Rajasic mode or a Tamasic mode. But with practice I can control mood of my mind. Even when these circumstances are not conducive, Bhagavan said, that becomes your predominant nature. Some people, no matter what it is, get angry. Some people, no matter what situation has come, enter the room and people will be all agitated. But that is because that is your basic nature.
Your basic nature is what is predominantly the life you are living and how you are reacting to the situations. And that makes up your mental texture. And as your mental texture, so is your faith. And as your faith, so will be your mental texture. So well go back and forth between who I am, what I have faith in, what my faith in what make me who I am. So what are the three types of Shraddha?
And this Shraddha is so powerful that it will lead your life. It will guide your life. Wherever I have my conviction that this is right. This is what will give me happiness. It will pursue that path. So our life is not really divided.
What I do in one aspect of my life does not affect the other aspect of my life. Even though we think, well, I compartmentalize my life -- my professional life is different from my personal life -- in reality there is nothing like that. Who you are will permeate through the entire life that you live, whether it is personal, professional, social, or sacred.
So Bhagawan said that thats very important. That you control the texture of your mind. Because that will exhibit your qualities no matter what you are doing. And therefore he said that even to something as simple as Ahar food also you will pursue according to the mental makeup of yours. So in the beginning we had talked about three types of people. What type of food they will like.
That is, something which will give nourishment, is life-giving, promotes health. When youre Rajasic, you will like something which is tasty, feel-good food, comfort food. As soon as the word comfort comes, you know its not really healthy. There is a restaurant in downtown that specializes in comfort food. I finally realized its all loaded with calories.
Thats why its good. I dont know why Bhagavan made it that way -- why cant comfort food be healthy? I always question why fried food is not the healthiest food. So up till now people have been saying low-fat milk, skim milk, low fat.
I just read article in New York Times said the whole milk is now rising in popularity. Because now the research says the whole milk is actually healthier than your skim milk. Still he said the American association, whatever the doctors recommend that you should have the low calorie diet. But the low calorie diet is gradually losing its glitter. So Bhagavan said that the person with Sattvic mood will find something which is nourishing and health giving. Rajesh will find something which tastes good and comfort food and its a tamasic.
Will get anything that is available. Does not matter whether it is good or bad. Then we said even the Yajna they perform in a broader sense. All my efforts are basically offered in the Yajna of my life. My life is a Yajna and I am offering all my efforts into it to achieve something good. Bhagawan saying the Yajna is for the greater good.
Even when I consider that Im doing something for the greater good it will be all as per my mental makeup. Even though I may have good intentions, I may end up doing something which may not be helpful to others. The road to hell is paved with good intentions -- I think the Rolling Stones or somebody said that. So sometimes, even though I have good intentions, my mental makeup will make me put efforts in a place where I feel right. They may not be right.
Therefore he says the Sattvik will put efforts where it is. He has figured out what is the right way to put actions. With faith, with guidance that he will put his effort. When I buy furniture, Im so impatient. Lets not worry about the instructions. Lets start putting it together.
Halfway I realize that I missed a couple of steps. I have to go back and undo it. Bhagavan said the sattvic person will find out the right way to do it first. Whatever he does, hell follow the proper method. A rajasic person will say lets get it done. Right or wrong, lets just get it done.
Because I want a result instantaneously -- that which gives me a result instantaneously, thats what I want to do. You dont have patience to go through this step by step, or Vidhi Purvakam. So because we want instantaneous results, I sing a song and people who are just like me, who dont know what music is, say: great, you are doing very well. Thats what I was looking for.
So thats Rajasic Yajna -- without any method but with a result, a fruit, in mind. And then the last one we have seen: Yajna where I dont even have faith in it, but its supposed to be done as per societys norm, or people think Im not doing right, so lets do it anyway. Its like a factor of safety before an exam -- go to the temple. I know thats not really going to help, but you might as well do it because there is no harm. Just as a factor of safety, maybe lets go to the temple and say: Bhagavan, take care, tomorrow I have an exam. Without faith, without any method, without any reason -- that Yajna, Bhagavan says, is Tamasic Yajna.
Then we came to the Tapas.
This faith affects ahara, yajna, tapa, and dana. So now we came to the Tapas part. Tapas, austerities, or as we loosely translate it, the disciplines which we follow. We discipline ourselves so that we can get some benefit out of it. We exercise routinely for our good health. I want to run a marathon -- I have to prepare myself.
So when we started this discussion, Bhagavan described three types of Tapas. First is at the physical level, next is Tapas at the speech level, and third is Tapas at the mental level, the thoughts level. So at the physical level:
In my activities, Bhagavan described worship of the Devas, Dwijah, Prajnah, and Guru -- deities, divine beings, twice born, wise people, and your guru. Ahimsa and Shaucham are considered Sharira Tapas. All of us, at some level or other, try to do that in our activities.
Next, speech: whatever I speak is non-agitating to others, it is truth but sweet-sounding truth, and it is beneficial to others. Thats Tapas at the speech level.
And then Tapas at the mind level, where my mind is silent and not creating unnecessary noise in the background. At the thought level, my thoughts are disciplined. My thoughts are always about my highest goal, which is to achieve that oneness with God, as we call it. But in reality, what we are looking for is unbroken happiness.
When I achieve a state where my happiness remains permanent -- its not temporary, its not coming and going -- Bhagavan said thats at the thought level. We know that most of us try at the physical level. The majority of people will fall into a category where they are trying their Tapas at the actions level. Where we fail is at the speech level, because we think that saying something is not hurting anybody.
Im Ahimsa-minded, but I say things that will hurt other people. Im not hitting him, Im not hurting him -- Im just saying things. We hear this in the media all the time these days. But Bhagavan said thats also very harmful, and therefore very important to watch. So the majority will stop at the physical level of Tapas in actions, but fail to do it at the speech level.
Then out of the remaining, there are few who try hard to be at the speech level, but most of us fail at the thought level. Because I think nobody knows what Im thinking. Nobody has any clue what Im thinking. Only my outward actions and my speech are the things people are noticing or judging me from. Most of our lives were doing things for others to judge us by, right? Thats why I said all marketing works very well.
Because all these people in marketing psychology figured out we never think about what this will look on me. Were only thinking about what it looks on others. So when we look at Tom Cruise wearing a suit which looks good on him, so I think it looks good on him, it should look good on me. So we try to judge ourselves by reflecting in the mirror of the society. And we think that what I am thinking in my mind nobody knows. And therefore we fail to do Tapas at the thought level.
But Bhagavan said all three, when performed together, will yield the good results. So the next verse says: Shraddhaya Paraya Taptam Tapah Trividham Naraihi Aphalakankshi Bhih Yuktaihi Sattvikam Parichakshate. A man with firm devotion -- Shraddhaya Paraya -- with firm faith, when a person is practicing all these three Tapas -- Trividham, all three -- and Aphalakankshi, he has no particular gain in mind. When Im doing Tapas also, I shouldnt be expecting a particular result, because I must have complete faith in the Karma Phaladata -- that if I put my efforts, the results will be there.
So I constantly hear from my staff: Rajan, I dont think that when we come on Sunday and work, anybody is appreciating it. I said, but I dont even know that you came on Sunday. Did you put down your timesheet that you were here on Sunday?

These verses complete the teaching on tapas by introducing the most subtle and important level: mental austerity (manasa tapa). Krishna describes it as manah prasadah (serenity of mind), saumyatvam (gentleness), maunam (silence or contemplation), atma-vinigrahah (self-control), and bhava-samsuddhih (purity of intention). This is the deepest discipline because, as Krishna notes, most people may discipline their actions and even their speech, but fail at the level of thought - believing that no one knows what Im thinking. Yet inner noise eventually corrupts both speech and action. Sattvic tapas is performed with supreme faith, without desire for reward; rajasic tapas is done for satkaramana-pujartham - for honor, respect, and praise - and its results are chalam adhruvam (unstable and temporary).
This week, practice the discipline of mental silence. Set aside even five minutes daily to simply observe your thoughts without engaging them. Notice: Is your mind predominantly serene or agitated? When you perform good actions, is there a hidden desire for recognition? The teaching reveals that rajasic tapas - discipline performed for applause - yields only temporary, unstable results. Ask yourself honestly: Would I still practice this discipline if no one ever knew about it? Also examine bhava-samsuddhih (purity of intention): even if your actions appear sattvic and your speech is controlled, what is the quality of your underlying motivation? True mental austerity means your inner world matches your outer presentation.
